title: What Structural Geology Studies — Fundamentals of Structural Geology
description: This entry covers What Structural Geology Studies as part of the fundamentals of structural geology. In this field, stress and strain matters because forces per area and the deformation they produce in rocks. It is taught at the Foundations level of the teaching ladder, building from first principles toward professional practice, with each concept defined before it is used.
overview: Structural Geology is the field concerned with How rocks deform: folds, faults, and the architecture of mountains and basins. What Structural Geology Studies belongs to its essential core. Concretely: Stress and strain — forces per area and the deformation they produce in rocks. And Faults — normal, reverse, and strike-slip breaks accommodating crustal motion. Mastering this entry means being able to explain the topic in plain sentences, recognize it in real cases, and apply it alongside the neighboring ideas of the Foundations tier.
core_concepts: Stress and strain: forces per area and the deformation they produce in rocks.
Faults: normal, reverse, and strike-slip breaks accommodating crustal motion.
key_laws: Anderson's theory of faulting: fault type predicted by the orientation of principal stresses.
vocabulary: Strike and dip: the compass direction and tilt of a planar feature.
Throw: the vertical component of fault displacement.
methods: Field mapping: measuring orientations and contacts to build geologic maps.
history: Structural geology grew from 19th-century Alpine mapping and the great fold-thrust debates; Anderson's 1942 faulting dynamics gave it theory. Plate tectonics provided the driving engine, and seismic imaging now reveals structures kilometers deep.
